body.content: If the paired-case design reveals that panel members use information beyond the checklist, does that constitute 'genuine reasoning' or could it still be a form of learned pattern-matching that is not generalizable?

Counterfactual probe: construct pairs of evaluation cases that are identical on all checklist-relevant features but differ on a feature the checklist does not encode. If panel accuracy differs between the paired cases, members are using information beyond the checklist (genuine reasoning). If accuracy is identical, they are pure compliance. This creates a within-evaluation experimental design that directly tests the compliance-vs-reasoning distinction.
body.possible_next_move: Design a simulation that generates paired cases with checklist-relevant features held constant and a checklist-irrelevant feature varied, then compare panel accuracy on the paired cases.
body.why_keep_this: This is a concrete experimental design that could resolve the debate about whether a single evaluation can distinguish genuine reliability from mere compliance.

body.content: Can the paired-case counterfactual probe be implemented in real evaluation settings without the checklist authors being able to anticipate and encode the 'irrelevant' features?
